claim: The self-survey recorded 34 rows marked `_read_ok=true` across six leaves and 668 unique retrieved URLs, and the successful-read count was inflated by identity/content false successes.
The field-dossier experiment reduced entry size by 96.97% on the narrow fixture and 98.45% on the broad fixture.
The field-dossier fixtures preserved 51 of 51 and 280 of 280 manifest artifacts and 3 of 3 and 7 of 7 branch syntheses, respectively.
In a fresh-agent lookup diagnostic, the dossier recovered 7 of 7 requested facts while the flat production bundle recovered 6 of 7 because the latter omitted the exact rejected-path decision record.
On the narrow same-run fixture, the production bundle was 950,921 bytes and the field dossier was 28,782 bytes while preserving 51 of 51 manifest artifacts and 3 of 3 branch syntheses.

The experimental field dossier embeds branch syntheses, exposes material decisions and claim verdicts, keeps full reads out of default context while retaining references, and content-addresses the raw artifact manifest.
The field-dossier diagnostic changed only the handoff artifact and did not establish better retrieval, evidence truth, contradiction handling, or synthesis.
Production Aletheia specifies source-separated competing framings, an adversary branch, read-only leaf workers at deep tiers, and centralized bottom-up final synthesis.

This survey did not compare expected value across its seven proposed improvement planes or establish whether output hierarchy is the main epistemic bottleneck; the ordering is explicitly provisional project policy.
Retaining production's source-separated framing portfolio is provisional project policy; this survey did not compare it against a one-model prompt asking for alternative perspectives.
Production runs persist questions, evidence, notes, findings, decisions, claims, and verdicts as filesystem artifacts across context windows.
Production's final-brief claim audit hashes the brief, claim set, and verdict file and makes post-attestation edits detectable within the local artifact model.
Production report.py described its agent bundle as complete while omitting decisions, questions, answers, specifications, status, and proposal artifacts.

The self-survey recorded the expected ACM PaperTrail DOI 10.1145/3772318.3791101 as a successful read even though the persisted body identified itself as the unrelated 2011 GRADE paper DOI 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2011.03.017.

The self-survey recorded the expected ACM DOI 10.1145/3742413.3789079 as a successful read even though the persisted body identified itself as the unrelated 2023 GRADE paper DOI 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2023.03.003.
The methods branch counted a 1,952-character anti-bot page as a successful read.
During the self-survey, the default router classified a systematic-review and meta-research query as products_consumer and required explicit academic-channel overrides.
During the self-survey, Aletheia prefixed focused named-method searches with the generic phrase agent-facing field-survey, adding irrelevant lexical anchors to exact queries.
Production Aletheia can label a primary publisher document as lead_gen merely because it was discovered through a web-search channel, conflating discovery path with epistemic role.
Production's unlimited tier stops on agent-judged convergence and has a 512-node runaway backstop, but no validated recall estimator.
A prior Aletheia scope verifier expanded 17 writer-selected claims to 32, showing that a self-selected denominator omitted nearly half of that final answer's load-bearing scope.
A prior high-accuracy Aletheia run omitted its positive national headline inference from claims.jsonl even though the causal branch said the national net sign was not identified.
Production's run-level origin and echo score does not attach origin requirements or independent-origin verdicts to individual claims.
Production computes structural-origin clusters in addition to run-level origin and echo scoring, but this survey did not quantify whether clustering is more valid or predictive than domain counts.

On 11 portable read-identity cases, production's effective length predicate was correct on 7 with four false accepts, while the experimental identity gate was correct on all 11 with no false accepts or false rejects among five usable controls.
Offline replay of the identity gate over this run's 34 production-success rows retained 30 and rejected two exact identity mismatches, one anti-bot interstitial, and one arXiv error shell.
The experimental identity gate records expected and observed identity, content state, content hash, resolver method, and preserved attempt path, and a retry does not overwrite the first wrong body.
The semantic read-identity branch passed its exact-defect diagnostic but remains unpromoted pending broader calibration and resolver-recovery tests.
The semantic read-identity branch passed 164 of 164 repository tests, compared with 156 of 156 on production.
Across 260 controlled configurations, a multi-agent scaling study reported outcomes ranging from positive 80.8% on decomposable financial reasoning to negative 70.0% on sequential planning.
The same multi-agent scaling study found that independent teams amplified trace errors more than centralized coordination.
Under equal token budgets, Tran and Kiela found a single agent best or statistically tied at usable budgets on two multi-hop reasoning tasks.
Anthropic reports that its multi-agent research system outperformed its single-agent setup by 90.2% on an internal breadth-oriented evaluation while using roughly 15 times the chat tokens.
Anthropic identifies tightly coupled work with many dependencies or shared context as a poor fit for parallel multi-agent research.
The combined multi-agent evidence supports parallelizing independent high-entropy discovery while centralizing dependent reasoning, verification, and final synthesis.
On BrowseComp-Plus, changing GPT-5 retrieval from BM25 to Qwen3-Embedding-8B raised accuracy from 55.90% to 70.12% while mean search calls fell from 23.23 to 21.74.

A separate deep-research ranking study reported accuracy of 0.572 for passage BM25 and 0.689 for BM25 followed by monoT5-3B reranking, with higher recall and fewer search calls for the reranked system.
In that ranking study, keyword-rich agent queries favored lexical retrieval while translation to natural-language questions improved neural retrieval and reranking on the tested benchmark.
FAIR-RAG's 200-case error analysis attributed 32.5% of failures to retrieval, 31.0% to generation after correct evidence, and 24.5% to the sufficiency controller.

In Greenhalgh and Peacock's 495-source audit of a complex review, 30% of included sources came from the predefined protocol, 51% from snowballing, and 24% from personal knowledge or contacts, with overlap between categories.
Greenhalgh and Peacock support adaptive backward/forward citation expansion on complex topics but do not establish snowballing as necessary for every narrow query.
The reproduced source-role defect supports storing discovery channel separately from document type and epistemic role.
A strong expected-versus-observed identifier mismatch must set automatic read success to false even when the fetched body is long and readable.
The exact resolver fields, title thresholds, and full read-state taxonomy remain experimental contracts rather than validated field-wide requirements.
GRADE inconsistency guidance distinguishes direction and magnitude of effects, precision and confidence-interval overlap, and the clinical or methodological context of heterogeneity.
GRADE guidance warns that fixed I-squared thresholds are arbitrary or context-dependent and cannot by themselves interpret inconsistency.
The 2025 weighted-CCA paper states that double-counting primary studies can magnify findings and skew conclusions.
Pieper and colleagues found that only 32 of 60 overviews mentioned overlapping reviews and introduced corrected covered area to quantify overlap.
Low overall review overlap can conceal concentrated duplicate information in particular primary studies.

The prior high-accuracy run demonstrates that supported factual premises do not validate a load-bearing inference when the inference is omitted from verification and contradicts an identification gap.
The proposed atomic claim/evidence graph and its complete field list remain unvalidated target architectures, although exact final-prose reconciliation is supported by prior failures.
MindSearch models web information seeking as a dynamically extended graph of decomposed questions rather than a fixed question tree.
Co-STORM updates a question-linked mind map as information and user feedback arrive.
Using a revision-capable question graph as Aletheia's semantic model while retaining directories as a navigation projection remains an unvalidated transfer hypothesis.

Treating a revision-capable graph as potentially better than the directory tree for Aletheia's semantic representation is an unvalidated project hypothesis; this survey did not compare the representations.
Booth catalogued eight possible stopping approaches for systematic searching and found little comparative evidence validating them.
No source successfully reviewed in this run validated a signal as an open-web completeness certificate, and Brave coverage was degraded.
The proposed multi-signal stop card is an observability contract to test, not a demonstrated recall proof.
W3C PROV defines a domain-neutral provenance model centered on entities, activities, agents, and relations such as use, generation, and derivation.
OpenHands reports an immutable event-sourcing core with low persistence and replay overhead and fewer system-attributable failures as part of a broader agent-system redesign.
Provenance records lineage but does not by itself establish that a claim is true.
Reflexion reports that retaining verbal feedback in episodic memory can improve agents on sequential decision-making tasks without updating model weights.
ExpeL reports that retained cross-task experience can improve agent performance but that adding plausible reflections hurt one HotPotQA setting, likely because those reflections hallucinated.
The exact event-ledger and negative-memory-card schemas proposed for Aletheia remain unvalidated transfers rather than established requirements.

This brief explicitly adopts, as project policy rather than an evidence-established universal rule, recording tool failures and empty index results as execution or coverage gaps instead of scientific null results.
HiAgent increased average success from 21% to 42% while reducing context tokens by 35.02% in its reported evaluation.
In HiAgent's ablation, removing on-demand retrieval of prior trajectory details reduced success by 10 percentage points.
WebWeaver's section-scoped writing system reported citation accuracy rising from 86.73% to 93.37% and citation support from 90.95% to 98.73% relative to its whole-memory writer comparison.
WebWeaver's ablation supports focused, section-addressed evidence as the operative mechanism in its tested writing setup rather than hierarchy by itself.

A July 2026 long-context-agent study found that a flat prepared index helped at larger corpus scale, while an always-loaded second routing level often reduced accuracy with some large-corpus open-QA exceptions.
The book-QA study and two-fixture dossier diagnostic motivate testing one bounded map with deeper artifacts on demand but do not establish that policy across field-survey domains.
A longer report or larger retrieved-source count does not by itself establish higher research quality.
The field dossier should remain experimental and should not be promoted on the basis of its first diagnostic.
A prior one-topic Aletheia bakeoff explicitly reported that retrieval luck, rather than architecture alone, explained much of its observed gap.
In a prior dynamic-outline comparison, the preferred candidate persisted 97 read artifacts versus 41 for baseline despite equal configured rounds, so the comparison was not cost-matched.
LLM judges exhibit position bias that can change pairwise evaluation outcomes.
MT-Bench documents order inconsistency, limited reasoning ability, and sensitivity to answer style among LLM judges.
LLM evaluators can prefer outputs associated with their own model family, creating self-preference bias.
MT-Bench mitigates position bias by judging each response pair in both orders and only declaring a winner when the same answer is preferred twice.

The proposed hidden criteria, topic mix, repeat count, downstream tasks, activation checks, paired intervals, and explicit inconclusive rule remain project gates to validate rather than externally established necessities.
One mechanism per branch is this project's default attribution discipline, not the only valid experimental design; prespecified factorial or feature-off ablations are alternatives.
The claim-evidence-ledger branch at commit 35fb82a implements a ledger candidate and tests outside production; its quality effect remains an open promotion question.
The accuracy-observability branch at commit 2edfffb implements tracked-read and run-observability hardening outside production.
The production tag aletheia-prod-v0.5.0-openai.1 points to runtime commit addfaf6, while the named experimental candidates remain outside production.

The cited multi-agent, writing-memory, and long-context studies use different tasks and designs and do not jointly test a ranking of architecture-task alignment, focused context, and agent or tree count for field surveys.
Requiring each experimental branch to preserve its hypothesis, activation trace, observed cost, result, falsifier, and promotion rationale is an explicit unvalidated project release policy.

The epistemic compiler, influence and echo maps, counterfactual dossier queries, compression-loss audits, and calibrated exploration portfolios are unvalidated experimental ideas rather than implemented Aletheia capabilities.
Rejecting more hierarchy as the main fix is current project policy based on conditional examples, not a universally validated rule for field surveys.

Several source-separated branch findings recur on typed evidence, provenance, selective context, primary resolution, explicit gap state, centralized reconciliation, and layered output, but that thematic recurrence is not claim-level independent corroboration.
Brave was degraded during the survey because no API key was configured, and GitHub operated through an unauthenticated rate-limited pool with transient failures recorded in branch traces.
This run did not quantify language, book, newsroom, domain-specialist, or user-organization coverage, so the degree of under-sampling is unknown.
The run's methods artifacts are visibly academically and technically concentrated, but the degree of corpus under-sampling was not measured.

Among sources successfully retrieved in this run, no controlled cross-domain layered-dossier-versus-flat-bundle study was located; degraded Brave coverage prevents treating that as a universal absence claim.

Among sources successfully retrieved in this run, no validated universal open-domain origin ontology or open-web stopping policy with a demonstrated recall guarantee was located; no targeted absence protocol was preserved.
This survey did not verify an integrated experiment covering the complete proposed evidence, control, and delivery architecture, which is a scope limitation rather than proof that none exists.

The immediate sequence—retain identity experimental, harden whole-answer claim coverage next, test retrieval and reranking third, and defer question graphs and stop control—is a risk-based project judgment rather than an evidence-ranked comparative expected-value result.
The closing aim to test wider reach, richer output, and durable memory is an authorial project purpose, not a forecast that those outcomes have been or will be achieved.
